newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: The Israeli shekel closed almost unchanged against the basket of foreign currencies but rose slightly against the dollar in quiet trading, dealers said.
"Trading was extremely quiet today and nothing happened. The central bank did not intervene in the market until the setting of the representative rate," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"Right after the setting of the representative rate the basket fell lower than 7.0 percent below the slope," he said.
"The Bank of Israel intervened on a very low scale just after the setting of the rate," said another dealer.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of foreign currencies, representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1440 against 3.1470 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5422 shekels against 3.5423 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8831 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8886 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.1235 shekels per mark against 2.1190 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1440 shekels.
